surface_mechanism_description: The HfO2 nucleation is independent of the crystallographic orientation of the substrate and is mainly determined by the thickness and, hence, the OH density of the O3/H2O wet chemical oxide. The initial correlation can be explained in terms of OH coverage of the surface. With the wet chemical oxides growing in islandlike structures, the surface of the substrate is only partially covered by oxide and therefore has only a limited OH density. Both oxide thickness and OH density increase as the islands grow larger, until eventually the surface is completely covered by oxide and the number of reactive OH sites is at a maximum.
evidence: The nucleation of HfO2 by ALD HfCl4/H2O strongly depends on the presence of reactive surface sites on the silicon substrate. Insufficient amounts of these sites can limit the HfO2 deposition to less than a monolayer per ALD cycle, affecting layer properties, such as density, uniformity, and electrical performance. An appropriate silicon surface pretreatment can enhance the number of surface sites and hence improve growth of the dielectric. The most continuous ALD layer-by-layer growth from HfCl4 and H2O has been reported on SiO2 layers grown by wet chemical oxidation of the substrate as these oxides contain high OH densities. Because these SiO2 layers tend to grow in an islandlike mode, the surface of the thinnest oxides will only have partial oxide coverage and, therefore, a limited OH density. As the islands grow larger, this will lead to an increase in oxide coverage and the associated OH termination of the silicon substrate.
